claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with: **Do you have a child or children that you're responsible for?** If yes, could you tell me how many children you have and their ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I have one child - Alex, who's 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Now I need to understand a bit more about Alex's situation.

**Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education or approved training?** For example, is Alex still in school, college doing A-levels or similar qualifications, or in an approved vocational training program?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in school or college anymore. They've finished with education.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few more questions to understand Alex's situation fully.

**Is Alex currently working, and if so, how many hours per week does Alex work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all currently.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Let me ask another important question about Alex's circumstances:

**Does Alex receive any benefits in their own right?** For example, does Alex claim Universal Credit, Income Support, or any other benefits as their own claimant?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in their own right.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I need to ask about your own circumstances:

**Are you currently living in the UK, and are you responsible for Alex (meaning Alex lives with you or you contribute to their upkeep)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Let me ask one more important question:

**Is Alex registered with HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) or with Jobcentre Plus as looking for work or available for work?** In other words, has Alex signed on or registered as seeking employment?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't registered or signed on anywhere looking for work.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for answering all my questions. Let me now assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit based on the information you've provided.

From what you've told me:
- Alex is 16 years old
- Alex is not in full-time non-advanced education or approved training
- Alex is not working
- Alex doesn't receive any benefits in their own right
- Alex lives with you in the UK
- Alex is not registered with HMRC or Jobcentre Plus as seeking work

Let me make my assessment now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why: Child Benefit can be claimed for children under 16, or for young people aged 16 to 19 if they're in approved full-time non-advanced education or approved training. Since Alex is 16 and has finished education and is not in approved training, Alex doesn't meet the qualifying conditions for Child Benefit.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future - for example, if Alex returns to full-time education, starts an approved training program, or registers with HMRC/Jobcentre Plus as seeking work - you may become eligible at that point. In that case, you would need to reapply or notify HMRC of the change in circumstances.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
